findings.title: Record-initial whole establishes a continuing topic
findings.actual_claim: A complete whole in a record’s first field introduces an active item/material topic that later compatible fields inherit until an independently visible topic change.
findings.tested_or_not_tested: Not independently tested. GDT596 reconstructs 254 authored working clauses from visible type/reference decisions, while GDT594 assigns occurrence-local defaults and distinguishes local carryover from reset; neither independently binds historical topic identity or record boundaries. Repeated category or a coherent article rendering is not an individual topic endpoint.
findings.countermodel: The initial whole is a positional opener or inherited renderer choice; later fields follow section, host, or record length without topic continuity. A topic can also shift silently, so continuity failure would not refute all record organization.
findings.reopening: Freeze record boundaries and topic/owner changes independently on at least five physical folios, exclude line-end assumptions, and compare candidate initial wholes with structural/opaque opener controls. Require held-field continuity and fewer unexplained owner switches beyond position, section, host class, and record length.

findings.title: Prior mention switches a whole from definite to anaphoric use
findings.actual_claim: A candidate whole changes reference status after the same owner/item has already been introduced: later mentions retain that owner without a new introduction cue, while first mentions cue introduction.
findings.tested_or_not_tested: Not tested as prior-owner conditioning. GDT573 mechanically pronounizes later repetitions of the same fully expanded argument within a card; GDT596 reports 70 anaphoric and 184 definite forms from its phrasebook; GDT594 reports local/reset occurrence defaults. These are authored or inherited rendering decisions, not independent owner/reference annotations. GDT220 and GDT169 show that proximity or page-level referent patterns do not supply singular ownership.
findings.countermodel: A fixed lexical or structural role recurs with or without a cue; repeated category does not entail repeated individual. A later occurrence may be a new owner of the same class, so a cue-rate difference cannot be interpreted without independently bound owner identity.
findings.reopening: Blindly annotate owner/reference history across five physical folios, then match first-owner and later-same-owner occurrences by record position and section. Test the preregistered 70% later-owner retention and 20-point first-mention cue gap; failure challenges this article-like switch only, not reference generally.
